what_its_for: Aminocaproic acid helps stop or prevent excessive bleeding. It works by blocking the natural process in your body that breaks down blood clots, helping clots stay in place and keeping you from bleeding too much. It is used for serious bleeding problems, often after surgery or injury, or in people with certain bleeding disorders.
how_to_take: Aminocaproic acid comes as a tablet, syrup (liquid), or as an injection given by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. Take the tablet or liquid form by mouth, with or without food. If the liquid upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Measure the liquid carefully using the dosing cup or syringe provided — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your condition, weight, and how you respond to the medicine. A common adult starting dose is 5 grams (5,000 mg) taken all at once, followed by 1 to 1.25 grams (1,000–1,250 mg) every hour. The total daily dose usually does not exceed 30 grams. For children, dosing is based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store tablets and liquid at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medications out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine past the expiration date printed on the label. If you need to dispose of unused medicine, ask your pharmacist about the best way to do so safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking hormonal birth control pills (oral contraceptives) or hormone replacement therapy at the same time as aminocaproic acid without talking to your doctor, as the combination may increase the risk of dangerous blood clots. Avoid activities that could cause injury or bleeding while on this medication. Do not drink alcohol without checking with your doctor first. Tell all your healthcare providers that you are taking this medicine before any procedure or surgery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency medical help if you experience: sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing up blood (signs of a blood clot in the lungs); pain, swelling, redness, or warmth in one leg (signs of a blood clot in the leg); sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking (signs of a stroke); muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored (tea or cola-colored) urine (signs of muscle breakdown); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; low blood pressure, dizziness, or fainting; worsening bleeding that is not controlled.
when_it_works: Aminocaproic acid starts working relatively quickly — often within 1 to 2 hours of taking it. When given by IV in a hospital, it begins working even faster. However, the full benefit depends on your specific condition and how your body responds. Your doctor will monitor you closely to make sure the medicine is working properly.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy is not fully known, and it may pass into breast milk. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Kidney disease: This drug is mostly removed from the body through the kidneys. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may need to lower your dose or monitor you more carefully. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially the risk of blood clots, and should be monitored closely. Children: Dosing in children is carefully calculated based on body weight, and this medicine should only be used under close medical supervision in this group.
